item.title: Mini Crackme — 2026-09-11 (Windows x86-64)
item.description:
Challenge: rcx points to a 4-byte ASCII buffer (Windows x64 convention). Find a 4-character string that makes check return 1.
check: xor eax, eax ; sum = 0 xor edx, edx ; i = 0 .loop: movzx r8d, byte [rcx+rdx] add eax, r8d ; sum += buf[i] inc edx cmp edx, 4 jl .loop cmp eax, 394 ; compare to target sum jne fail mov eax, 1 ret fail: xor eax, eax ret
Answer: "abcd"
The loop walks the 4 bytes at [rcx] with movzx/add, accumulating their raw ASCII values into eax -- no shifting or weighting, just a plain running total, repeated exactly four times via inc edx/cmp edx,4/jl. After the loop, cmp eax, 394 / jne fail demands the four bytes sum to exactly 394. 'a'+'b'+'c'+'d' = 97+98+99+100 = 394, so "abcd" clears the check and check returns 1 (other 4-byte combinations summing to 394 also work).
